subject: Traffic smoothing policy conflict — BlueLake Health latency & 429s
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily@bluelakehealth.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: sre-team@bluelakehealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike + 429s — suspecting capacity gating

Marcus / Monica,

We started seeing a sustained latency increase and intermittent 429s against your hosted endpoint for the past 20 minutes. Traffic pattern didn't change on our side — same request mix and QPS. The impact is visible across a couple of important workflows (document ingestion + patient summary generation).

Attached is a sample log segment showing the 429s and client-side timing. TL;DR: 90th p50 latency up ~3x, occasional 429 returned to our users. We need an immediate explanation and mitigation plan — this is customer-impacting.

Can your team confirm whether any quota/burst policy changes were deployed this morning? If there’s an emergency bypass or temporary relax we can use that now, please advise.

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Head of Integrations, BlueLake Health
emily@bluelakehealth.com

Attachments: bluelake-429-sample.log (text/plain)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily@bluelakehealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike + 429s — suspecting capacity gating

Emily — thanks for the sample, and I'm sorry for the disruption. We see the same anomalies on our side and have pulled the initial traces. Early read shows a safety valve engaged on the tenant-level smoothing policy that started to queue/bucket requests when short-term bursts exceeded the configured window. It looks like the smoothing window was narrowed in last night's policy rollout which made the valve much more sensitive to bursty traffic.

Immediate actions we've kicked off:
- Rolling back the policy change to last-known-good (ETA ~18 minutes).
- Opening a 1-hour emergency bypass for BL-471 so requests go to the standard rate controller (no smoothing enforcement).
- Captured and attached our policy snapshot for the morning rollout.

I'll follow up as soon as the rollback completes. If you need us to flip the bypass now, confirm and we'll do it immediately.

— Monica
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Attachments: policy-snapshot-20290514.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production latency spike + 429s — suspecting capacity gating

Team — forwarding BlueLake's report. Monica indicates a policy rollout narrowed the smoothing window; if that's true we need an RCA and a clear exec summary ASAP. BlueLake is a high-priority customer (on Dedicated discussion, DL-471).

Immediate asks:
1) Confirm rollback status and whether the bypass is active now.
2) How many other tenants were affected by the same policy rollout today?
3) Short-term mitigation options (rollback + credits + communication) and recommended timeline for full remediation.

Looping in Lauren for any commercial guidance re: credits / SLA implications and Soojin for reliability assessment.

Marcus
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency spike + 429s — suspecting capacity gating

Update after quick triage: the engineering rollout pipeline pushed a narrower smoothing window at 02:47 UTC this morning as part of a global policy change intended to reduce long-tail token costs. The change passed canary but the canary traffic didn't include some tenant burst profiles (e.g., BlueLake’s periodic ingestion bursts).

Findings:
- The smoothing window decreased from 10s to 2s for the tenant-level safety valve for a subset of customers.
- When queuing exceeded internal thresholds, requests were short-circuited with 429s rather than gracefully spilling to queued execution — that's misaligned with our intended degradation mode.
- The rollback to 10s was triggered at 08:40 PDT and the emergency bypass enabled at 08:44 PDT. Metrics show error rate falling within 6 minutes and latency recovering within ~10 minutes for most flows.

Next steps I recommend (short & medium term):
A) Postmortem: full root-cause on canary selection criteria, rollout gating, and the controller fallback behavior. (Owner: Reliability — deliverable in 48hrs)
B) Immediate policy change: change degradation from hard-429 to degraded-queueing for tenant safety valve (owner: Runtime team) — target 2 weeks.
C) Customer remediation: offer 2 weeks of service credits, share a technical summary + timeline, and schedule a joint postmortem call with BlueLake.

I can prepare a technical one-pager and a timeline for A/B if you want me to draft it for execs.

— Soojin
Director, Reliability Engineering
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Emily Chen <emily@bluelakehealth.com>
Cc: support@redwood.ai, accounts@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 13:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike + 429s — suspecting capacity gating

Emily — thanks for raising this and for partnering while we investigated. Per Soojin's update: the rollback + bypass are active and we’ve confirmed recovery across your affected workflows. We're scheduling a 30-minute joint postmortem at 16:00 PDT today to walk through the technical details and remediation plan.

Commercial commitments: we will credit BlueLake Health for the impacted window (2 hours total), and Lauren from Accounts will follow up with the formal credit memo and a short letter of apology. Marcus and I will join the postmortem meeting.

Action items for today: 
- 16:00 PDT postmortem call — invite sent (link in thread).
- Soojin: one-pager on controller fallback behavior + targeted ETA for changing degradation mode.
- Monica: attach the final policy snapshot and confirm the tenants list that saw the change.
- Marcus: executive summary for leadership (one-paragraph + ask for approval on credit).

Appreciate the patience — we take this seriously and will share the full RCA.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
